steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease 24 muffin cups or line cups with paper liners.
To make the pumpkin cupcakes: Sift flour, baking powder, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, allspice, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl. Set aside.

Beat white sugar, 1/2 cup butter, and brown sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in pumpkin puree and milk. Gently mix in flour mixture until just combined. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each 3/4 full.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops spring back when lightly pressed, about 25 minutes. Cool in the pans for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool, about 20 minutes.

To make the frosting: Beat cream cheese and 1/4 cup butter together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Beat in confectioners' sugar, a little at a time, until incorporated. Add vanilla extract and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon; beat until fluffy.
Frost cooled cupcakes with cream cheese frosting.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: Deliciously moist pumpkin cupcakes topped with a creamy cinnamon cream cheese frosting. Easy to make and perfect for fall and holiday celebrations.

review.reviewBody:
I just made these cupcakes and they were by far some of the best I have had in a long time. They taste and look like they were purchased from a cupcake store. I did however read a lot of the reviews, and took all the tips into consideration. Here are the changes I made for perfection:
1. Reduced Heat to 350 and baked 22 minutes.
2. Put 1 whole can of pumpkin puree (equals about 1 1/2 cups)
3. Used 1/2 cup vegetable oil instead of butter.
4. used "heaping" spoonfuls of the spice, and left out the clove.
5. used 1 tsp salt (instead of half)
6. For the frosting only used about 2 cups sugar instead of 3.

I am already heading out to the store to buy ingrediants to make these again!

OMG! I made these for a Halloween party and they were a HUGE hit! They were light and fluffy and absolutely delightful. I used oil instead of butter, added the whole 15 oz. can of pumpkin and baked the cupcakes for about 22 minutes. I piped on the frosting, so I needed an extra 1/4 of the frosting recipe. If you just spread it on, you will be fine with the recipe amount as is.

I made this recipe twice, with the same basic changes both times. I used the entire can of pumpkin puree and heaping spoons of unexpired spices (I suspect the people complaining that the cake is bland are using old spices that lack potency). I baked for a bit longer due to the extra puree, but the cake turned out moist and good.

The first time I made this recipe, I used half that batter for cupcakes for my family and the other half as a small cake in a foil pan as part of a meal for a sick friend. The second time, I bake it in two cake pans and made it into a layer cake. All turned out great. 

It would also be good without the frosting as sweet muffins or with some streusel topping.

I love love love these cupcakes! It can be so hard to find a pumpkin cupcake recipe that isn't dense, and ends up being more muffin-like than cake-like--but this recipe nails it! They're light, fluffy, cakey, and delicious! My changes were to use 1 1/2 cups pumpkin puree, upped the cinnamon to 2 tsps and upped the ginger to 1 tsp, and used sour cream in place of milk. I baked these at 350 for 25 minutes and got 21 perfectly sized cupcakes. For the frosting, I didn't measure the amount of cinnamon I added (just eyeballed it), but otherwise followed the recipe as written. This made enough to generously frost most of the cupcakes (only two had a thinner layer of frosting than the others). These also taste great the next day or two after making them! Thanks so much for sharing your recipe!

I followed another reviewer's recommendation, and added two cans of pumpkin, 3 eggs, and doubled the spices. These were so good! They were very fluffy, pumpkin-y and all good fall things. I did not include the frosting, as these were yum on their own, and my toddlers did not need the extra sugar. These were a huge hit, and I will make these bad boys again. Thanks for sharing!

These cupcakes turned out excellent. They are moist and don’t stick to the cupcake wrapper. I did add chocolate chips and baked at 350 for 20-21 minutes and got about 20 cupcakes out of the batter. Overall, really happy with this recipe and will definitely make again in the near future!!!

these are good but I hate having leftover pumpkin from a 15 oz can so after reading the reviews on the dryness, I used the whole can. used 2 1/4 tsp pumpkin pie spice instead of the individual spices. replaced the butter with applesauce. made 22 nice sized cupcakes. held the cinnamon out of the frosting, and added a touch of maple extract with the vanilla instead. I also added vanilla to the batter. made a very nice cupcake.

These are just the thing to start off October! I did read reviews as well and take that into consideration, made the following changes; baked at 350 for about 22-25 minutes. Used 1/2 cup I believe of vegetable oil rather than butter and left out the cloves. The frosting I followed exactly and best cream cheese frosting I’ve made to date! Very happy with the results will be making again!

I used the whole 15oz can of Pumpkin Purée and added a Tbs of Vanilla. Was generous with the spices, too and used oil in place of butter. Baked at 350 for 22 mins. These were Fabulous! Made frosting with half cube butter, 4oz Cream Cheese, 1/4c milk, 2 tsp vanilla and added powdered sugar desired consistency.

I followed the cupcake recipe to a T. And I agree with previous poster that rating this recipe with changes is not a true rating of THIS recipe. I would have given this 3.5 stars if the option existed. My family and I "Liked it" and it was more than "It was okay". I did these as mini cupcakes (reduced the time to 15 minutes) and it yielded about 70 minis. I think I might try oil instead of butter next time. I'm fairly new to baking, and so I'm learning a lot by trial and error but don't know enough yet to get creative and try my own variations and substitutions. I did have to add more powdered sugar to the frosting because I over mixed and the frosting was too runny, but otherwise, I find the creaminess of the frosting as a good balance to the slightly dry recipe of the cupcake. In any event it is a hit with my family and one of my twins said it was her favorite cupcake I've made yet (and I've made quite a few!), so that's saying something, I guess. :D

I used squash i had frozen from last year instead of pumpkin, and I added about half a cup more. I also baked it in a Bundt pan for approximately 35 minutes and lightly glazed it, but otherwise I followed the recipe. I was a little worried when I added the milk, because it looked like it curdled, but after adding the flour, it came together and turned out nicely. Very tasty, though I think it could use some walnuts
Good for autumn

I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out great. Plenty of flavor and so fluffy! My powder sugar was stale so I didn't frost them and we ate them as muffins. Perfectly sweet even without the topping.
I make these every fall, and they NEVER disappoint! Probably my favorite dessert ever, and that’s really saying something. So moist and just sooooooo good!!

Everyone loved these! I made adjustments due to high altitude (just googled it), used the whole can of pumpkin purree and vegetable oil instead of butter, did not use cloves (per other helpful reviews). Super moist and flavorful! I got 20 cupcakes and just enough frosting using 2 cups of powerdered sugar.

Delicious! I made 12 cupcakes and 5 jumbo cupcakes. I made it as written, except I only used 2.5 c of powdered sugar. 12 cupcakes were ready in 20 minutes. Jumbo muffins took 5 more minutes. After putting on the frosting (I added 1 tsp of lemon juice), I sprinkled some cinnamon sugar to top. Btw, the recipe makes a lot of frosting!
Heading into March and I made these bad boys for the ladies, and 24 wasn't enough lol. A little extra butter helps

Made exactly as written and these cupcakes are delicious!!! Loved the cinnamon addition to the frosting! I made in a muffin pan, 9 large cupcakes and bake time was the same. Will do these again over the holidays.
I love these
Doubled the spices and used 3/4 tsp salt. Substiruted buttermilk.
